What NDT software actually has to do

NDT software has one core job: turn what a certified technician saw on the part into a signed, traceable report that a client, an authorized inspector or an auditor will accept without a phone call. Everything else, from scheduling to invoicing, only matters if that report is right. The best NDT software makes the correct report the easiest one to produce.

That sounds simple until you look at what a real inspection contractor in Texas, Louisiana or Alberta handles in a normal week: UT thickness surveys on a turnaround, radiography on a pipeline spread, MT and PT on structural welds at a fabrication shop, a PAUT or TOFD scope on a pressure vessel, and maybe an IRIS job on a heat exchanger bundle. Each method has different data, different acceptance criteria and a different reviewer who will pick it apart. Generic form builders treat all of these as the same form with different labels. Real NDT reporting software treats each method as its own report type with its own fields, its own numbering sequence and its own PDF layout.

This section walks through what the software has to capture for each method, the selection criteria that actually separate good tools from weak ones, and how the Atlantis NDT Reports app and our Digital Twin Reporting Software meet them. At the end we explain where the wider Atlantis ERP solution fits for companies that want the report connected to certifications, equipment calibration, dispatch and billing.

NDT reporting software, method by method

NDT reporting software earns its place when it knows the difference between a UT calibration table and an RT IQI placement. The Atlantis NDT Reports app ships with 17 report types, each with its own number sequence so your UT reports and your RT reports never share a counter.

MethodWhat the report has to captureHow Atlantis NDT Reports handles it
UT (shear/straight beam)Instrument, probe, calibration, reference block, indications and evaluationDedicated UT report with a probe calibration table and weld/job lines
UT thickness (UTT)Readings by location and direction, nominal and minimum valuesUTT report with readings recorded by direction
PAUTProbe, wedge, focal laws, scan plan, indicationsPAUT report with focal law data
TOFDProbe pair set-up, scan data, indicationsSeparate TOFD report type
RT and Computed RadiographySource, technique, IQI type and placement, film or plate detailsRT fields for source, technique, IQI type and placement; separate CR report type
MTTechnique, particle type, magnetisation detailsMT technique and particle type fields
PTPenetrant method, developer, dwell detailsPT method and developer fields
VTVisual findings, weld profile, photosVT report with photo capture
ECT, IRIS, MFLTube data, scan mode, item linesECT and IRIS report types; MFL with scan mode and item lines
PWHT, PMI, Hardness, Ferrite, HolidayTest values against a specificationEach is its own report type with its own sequence

Every report type shares the same backbone: weld or job lines with defect type and orientation, and an overall result of acceptable, not acceptable, or acceptable with remarks.

UT, UTT and PAUT reports

Ultrasonic work is where most reporting tools fall down, because the report is only as credible as the calibration behind it. A UT report without the probe, frequency, angle and reference block recorded is a report an authorized inspector can reject on sight. In the Atlantis UT report the probe calibration table sits inside the report itself, not in a separate spreadsheet someone has to attach later.

UT thickness surveys are a different animal. A turnaround crew may take hundreds of readings on piping and vessels, and the client wants them laid out so they can compare against the last survey. The UTT report records readings by direction so the grid comes out the way the client expects. The Atlantis ERP does not calculate inspection intervals or remaining life; that analysis belongs to the owner's integrity team or to our Atlantis Digital Twins platform, which trends thickness data in 3D.

PAUT reports carry focal law data so a reviewer can see what the scan actually covered. Because the equipment used on the job is tracked by serial number in the ERP, the report can be tied to an instrument and probe whose calibration status is known on the day of the inspection rather than guessed at when the client asks.

RT and computed radiography reports

Radiography reports are scrutinised harder than almost anything else a contractor issues, because the film or image is the evidence and the report is the map to it. The RT report in Atlantis captures the source, the technique, the IQI type and IQI placement, alongside weld lines with defect type and orientation. Computed Radiography has its own report type and its own number sequence.

For US radiography crews working under NRC or Agreement State licences, and Canadian crews working under CNSC requirements, the people side matters as much as the film. The employee NDT profile in the ERP records radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, and the Fleet app records whether a vehicle can carry radioactive sources along with its transport licence number and expiry. None of that replaces your radiation safety programme, but it means the office can see at a glance who is fit and qualified to be sent out on a shoot tonight.

On the report itself, references matter: work order, request, WPS, contract, drawing numbers, and the procedure and standard referenced, for example ASME Section V for technique and ASME B31.3 or API 1104 for acceptance, depending on the job. Atlantis captures these references on every report so a reviewer can trace the result back to the rules it was judged against.

MT, PT and VT reports

Surface methods look easy, which is why they generate so many sloppy reports. An MT report that does not say whether the technique was yoke, prods or coil, or whether particles were wet fluorescent or dry visible, is not a complete record. Atlantis MT reports capture the technique and particle type. PT reports capture the penetrant method and developer. These are the fields auditors ask about first.

VT is often the most photographed method on a job, and photos are where paper workflows break. The Atlantis offline field app lets a technician capture photos directly into the report draft, and marine-mode reports lay inspection photos out in a two-up grid in the PDF. For structural steel work under AWS D1.1 in the US or CSA W59 in Canada, being able to show the weld profile issue in a photo next to the finding saves a lot of back-and-forth with the fabricator.

Because surface methods are high-volume and low-margin, speed matters. A technician picking a method, filling the method-specific fields, capturing photos and signing on screen, all without signal, is the difference between reports going out the same day and reports going out next week.

ECT, IRIS, MFL, TOFD and specialist reports

Specialist methods need specialist fields. Eddy current and IRIS work on heat exchangers and boiler tubes, MFL on tank floors and tubes, TOFD on heavy-wall welds: each of these has its own report type in Atlantis. MFL reports carry scan mode and item lines, so a tank floor scan can be broken down by plate or zone rather than written up as one paragraph.

The same applies to what many contractors call the ancillary tests: PWHT records, PMI, hardness, ferrite and holiday or coating tests. These are frequently bolted onto an NDT package on fabrication and shutdown work, and they are often the reports that get lost because they sit outside the main NDT system. In Atlantis each has its own report type and number sequence, so a fabrication package for an EPC can contain RT, MT, PMI, hardness and PWHT records all produced from one place, with consistent numbering and headers.

If a method you perform is not on this list, for example a specialised leak testing record, a template for it is configured during implementation. Company templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML are versioned and carry your logo, header and footer, and Excel templates can be filled automatically by mapping fields to cells, which is useful when a client insists on their own spreadsheet format.

Review, approval and signatures

A report is not finished when the technician finishes it. It is finished when a qualified reviewer has checked it and it has gone to the client. The Atlantis report workflow runs draft, in progress, review, approved, sent. The inspector, reviewer and approver each sign, and there is space for a third-party or authorized inspector name and signature, which matters on code work where an AI from the jurisdiction or an owner's inspector witnesses the test.

This workflow is what separates NDT reporting software from a PDF generator. You can see which reports are stuck in review, which have been approved but not sent, and who signed what. When a client disputes a result six months later, you are not digging through email to find out which version went out.

For marine and offshore work, marine mode adds a vessel cover page and photo, inspection location and dates, and builds a PDF that merges the classification society certificate (from a library covering DNV, ABS, Lloyd's Register, BV, RINA, IRS and ClassNK), the inspector's Level II certificate and the calibration certificate. That is the pack a class surveyor on the Gulf Coast or in a Canadian shipyard expects to see, generated rather than assembled by hand. If you want to see a full review cycle on your own report formats, book a reporting demo.

Field capture that works without signal

Refineries, tank farms, offshore platforms and the inside of a vessel all have one thing in common: poor or no mobile signal. NDT software that needs a live connection forces technicians back to paper, and paper means retyping, and retyping means errors. The Atlantis field app is an installable web app that works offline. It stores drafts and photos on the device and syncs when the technician is back in range.

Inside the app a technician picks the method, fills the method-specific fields, captures photos, signs on screen and previews the PDF before submitting. A REST API behind it serves the jobs assigned to that technician and the equipment issued to them, so the report starts pre-linked to the job and the instrument rather than relying on someone typing a serial number correctly at the end of a twelve-hour shift.

This matters more for small and mid-sized contractors than for large ones. A large company can afford a data-entry clerk. A ten-technician shop in the Permian or in Fort McMurray usually cannot, and the owner ends up doing reports at night. Getting the report right at the point of inspection is the single biggest time saving most NDT companies will ever get from software.

Best NDT software: selection criteria that matter

The best NDT software for your company is the one that covers every method you perform with real method-specific fields, runs offline in the field, enforces review and approval, and connects the report to the technician's certification and the instrument's calibration. Everything else is secondary. Use this list when you compare options:

  • Method coverage: does each method you perform have its own report type and numbering, or is it one generic form?
  • Calibration inside the report: can the UT probe calibration, RT IQI data and instrument serial be captured in the report itself?
  • Offline field capture: can a technician finish a report with no signal and sync later?
  • Review workflow: is there a defined draft-review-approve-send cycle with signatures, including third-party inspectors?
  • Your templates: can reports come out on your letterhead, or on the client's spreadsheet format, without manual copying?
  • Certification link: will the system warn you if the technician's certificate is not valid?
  • Equipment link: will it warn you if the instrument assigned to the job is out of calibration?
  • Onward connections: does the report connect to the job, the timesheet and the invoice, or does it stop at a PDF?
  • Customization: when your biggest client changes their format, who changes the template and how quickly?

Tools that pass the first five criteria are good reporting tools. Tools that pass all nine are NDT software solutions that run the business around the report.

Non destructive testing software beyond the report: where the ERP fits

Non destructive testing software usually starts as a reporting problem and turns into a business problem. Once reports are digital, the next questions are: was the technician certified for that method on that date, was the instrument in calibration, and did the job get invoiced? That is where the Atlantis ERP solution comes in. The NDT Reports app is one app inside it.

Around the report, the ERP tracks technician certifications by scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level and method, with status computed automatically as active, expiring soon, expired or revoked, and warning tasks raised 90 days before expiry. Vision tests are tracked with the same care. Timesheets warn when a technician's certificate is not valid. Equipment and probes are tracked by serial number with calibration records and a calibration certificate register, and Team Assignments warns when assigned equipment is out of calibration and blocks double-booking of technicians and equipment serial numbers.

On the commercial side, quotes carry job type, site, dates and applicable codes, invoices carry job and PO numbers and split labour, equipment and consumables, and timesheet hours feed billing. The Procedures app holds your written practice and procedures with revision control and approval, so the procedure referenced on a report is the approved revision. You can browse each of these on the ERP apps overview or go straight to NDT Reports, Certificates and Asset Management.

Digital Twin Reporting Software and Atlantis Digital Twins

Some clients want more than a PDF. Owner-operators running large facilities increasingly want inspection findings placed on the asset so they can see where indications and thickness readings sit on a vessel, a piping circuit or a tank. That is what the Digital Twin Reporting Software and Atlantis Digital Twins are for: 3D visualisation of inspection data, damage and indication mapping, and thickness and remaining-life trends over time.

For a service company, this is a way to hand a client something more useful than a stack of reports, and a reason for that client to keep coming back to you for the next inspection. For an owner, it turns years of scattered reports into a picture of the asset. The two layers complement each other: the ERP and NDT Reports app produce the controlled, signed record; the digital twin makes that record easy to read in context.

You do not need both on day one. Most contractors start with reporting and certifications, then add dispatch and invoicing, then look at digital twin deliverables for their larger clients. Everything is set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, founded by an ASNT NDT Level III, and every setup is fully customizable. Pricing is quote on request; ask for a quote scoped to your methods.

NDT software solutions for US and Canadian contractors

North American NDT work runs on a specific set of codes and clients, and the software should reflect them. US contractors typically report against ASME Section V techniques with acceptance to ASME Section VIII, B31.1 or B31.3, AWS D1.1 for structural steel and API 1104 for pipeline welds. Canadian contractors add CSA W59 and CSA Z662, and deal with provincial authorities such as ABSA in Alberta and TSSA in Ontario. Every Atlantis report captures the procedure and standard references so that the code behind each result is on the page.

Certification schemes differ too. Most US employers certify to SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 under their own written practice, while Canadian technicians frequently hold NRCan certification under the ISO 9712-based CGSB standard. The Certificates app records all of these side by side, so a contractor working both sides of the border can see which technician holds which certificate for which method, and when it expires. Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training if you need to bring people up to Level I or II.

Integration matters for contractors who work inside large owner-operators. The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and can connect to SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation. If you want to see how your current reporting process would map across, request a walkthrough with a Level III.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT reporting software in 2026?

The best NDT reporting software is the one with a real report type for every method you perform, offline field capture, a signed review and approval workflow, and links to certifications and calibration. Atlantis NDT Reports covers 17 report types including UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, CR, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS and MFL, inside a fully customizable ERP.

Does Atlantis NDT software work offline?

Yes. The field app is an installable web app that stores drafts and photos on the device when there is no signal and syncs later. Technicians can pick the method, capture photos, sign on screen and preview the PDF offline.

Can reports come out in my client's format?

Yes. Company templates in Excel, Word, PDF and HTML are versioned and carry your logo, header and footer. Excel templates can be filled automatically by mapping report fields to cells, which covers clients who insist on their own spreadsheet.

What is the difference between NDT software and an NDT ERP?

NDT software often means reporting only. An NDT ERP connects the report to technician certifications, equipment calibration, dispatch, timesheets, quotes and invoices. Atlantis NDT Reports is one app inside the Atlantis ERP solution, so you can start with reporting and add the rest.

Does the software calculate inspection intervals or remaining life?

No, the ERP does not calculate inspection intervals or corrosion trends. Thickness and remaining-life trends are visualised in Atlantis Digital Twins, and the ERP records the inspection data and references.

How much does Atlantis NDT software cost?

Every setup is scoped to your methods, team size and integrations, so pricing is quote on request. The positioning is simple: affordable, accessible and fully customizable. Use the contact page to request a demo or a quote.
